questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. The group of students, B. along with the professor, C. were discussing the new findings D. in the research lab.
questions.solution:
The subject group is singular. Along with the professor does not change its number. Use was discussing, so segment C is incorrect.

**Answer: were discussing the new findings**

questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. She spoke B. so fastly that C. I could barely understand D. what she was saying.
questions.solution:
Fast serves as both adjective and adverb. Fastly is not the standard adverb, so segment B is incorrect.

**Answer: so fastly that**

questions.q:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate preposition:

The researchers accounted ___________ all variables before finalizing the data model.
questions.solution:
Account for means take into consideration or explain. The researchers accounted for all variables.

**Answer: for**

questions.q:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate verb:

She _____________ her position on the matter only after repeated questioning by the press.
questions.solution:
Clarified means made a position clear. It is the verb that fits explaining her view after questioning.

**Answer: clarified**

questions.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Pellucid
questions.solution:
Pellucid means clear or transparent. Clear is the matching synonym.

**Answer: Clear**

questions.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: **Querulous**
questions.solution:
Querulous means complaining or habitually dissatisfied.

**Answer: Complaining**

questions.q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: Out and about
questions.solution:
Out and about describes being active outside the home, rather than staying in or resting.

**Answer: Active and socializing**

questions.q: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: **Retired**
questions.solution:
Retired means withdrawn from active work. Active is the opposite in this context.

**Answer: Active**

questions.q: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: **Veracity**
questions.solution:
Veracity means truthfulness. Falsehood is its opposite.

**Answer: Falsehood**

questions.q: Which sentence contains a misspelled word?
options: Many believed the new millennium would bring great change, but some felt embarrassed when their predictions failed.
He didn't want to embarrass himself at the start of the new millenium.
The celebration of the millennium was truly unforgettable, though it did embarrass a few politicians.
She didn't expect the event to embarrass her during the millennium gala.
questions.solution:
The second option misspells millennium as millenium. Millennium has two n letters.

**Answer: He didn't want to embarrass himself at the start of the new millenium.**

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.

The student said, "I have been reading this book for a month, but I still do not understand the last chapter, which is the most crucial part."
options: The student said that he had been reading that book for a month, but he still did not understand the last chapter, which was the most crucial part.
The student said that he has been reading this bookfor a month, but he still does not understand the last chapter, which is the most crucial part.
The student said that he had been reading this book for a month, but he still did not understand the last chapter, which was the most crucial part.
The student said that he had been reading that book for a month, but he still does not understand the last chapter, which is the most crucial part.
questions.solution:
Backshift have been to had been, do not to did not, and is to was. Change this book to that book.

**Answer: The student said that he had been reading that book for a month, but he still did not understand the last chapter, which was the most crucial part.**

questions.q: Which sentence contains a misspelled word?
options: We went to a new restuarant downtown.
Is there a restaurant nearby that's open late?
They own the oldest restaurant in town.
questions.solution:
Restuarant reverses the order of the a and u. The correct spelling is restaurant.

**Answer: We went to a new restuarant downtown.**

questions.q:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

All the **__jury members was divided__** in their opinions.
options: All the jury member were divided
All the jury members were divided
All the jury were divided between their opinions
All juries have divided in their opinions
questions.solution:
Members is plural, so the verb must be were. The correct phrase is All the jury members were divided.

**Answer: All the jury members were divided**

questions.q:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

One should **__do ones' duty.__**
questions.solution:

questions.q:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

You must finish your homework.
options: Your homework must be finished by you.
Your homework must being finished by you.
Your homework must have been finished by you.
Your homework is must be finished by you.
questions.solution:
The passive form after must is be + past participle: Your homework must be finished by you.

**Answer: Your homework must be finished by you.**

questions.q: The phrase "enabling young aspirants to spar with grandmasters worldwide" functions as:
questions.solution:
Enabling introduces a present participle phrase. It describes how the activity supports young aspirants.

**Answer: Participle phrase**

questions.q: Identify the voice in "Initially conceived as a strategic simulation of warfare".
questions.solution:
Conceived is a past participle used in a reduced passive construction: it was initially conceived as a simulation.

**Answer: Passive voice**

questions.q: The word "meteoric" most nearly means:
questions.solution:
Meteoric means very rapid and striking, as in a meteoric rise. Rapid and spectacular is the closest meaning.

**Answer: Rapid and spectacular**

questions.q: The word "acumen" means:
questions.solution:
Acumen means sharp judgement or quick understanding.

**Answer: Sharpness in understanding**

questions.q:
Which of the following pairs of homonyms can be used to fill in the blanks most suitably?

The interior designer received a __________ from her client for choosing furniture that would perfectly __________ the walls and floors.
questions.solution:
A compliment is praise. To complement something means to match or enhance it. Therefore compliment, complement fits.

**Answer: compliment, complement**
